chain.title: The Same Print System
chain.desc: A vanilla oak trapdoor and four paper give four Classic Trapdoor Prints. Twelve of the seventeen trapdoor styles are print-gated exactly as the doors are, and the print is always made from the matching vanilla trapdoor.

chain.title: One Print, One Trapdoor
chain.desc: A Classic Trapdoor Print between two planks gives one trapdoor in that wood. Ten woods per print family, and the oak version is missing on purpose because vanilla already has it.

chain.title: Two Panes and Four Planks
chain.desc: Planks around glass panes, two at a time. The glass trapdoor is not print-gated and it is the parent of the barn trapdoor above it.

chain.title: Boards Over the Glass
chain.desc: A glass trapdoor with planks on top. It is the only trapdoor in the mod crafted from another trapdoor of the same mod, which makes it the one two-step recipe here.

chain.title: Logs, Not Planks
chain.desc: Logs around glass panes, two at a time - the bark-textured cousin of the glass trapdoor, in eleven woods.

chain.title: A Barrel Lid
chain.desc: A barrel ringed by four planks gives four Barrel Trapdoors, the only recipe in the mod that consumes a functional vanilla block.

chain.title: Bamboo Straight Through
chain.desc: Six bamboo in two rows. It is the only trapdoor here made from a raw material rather than planks, logs or a print.

chain.title: Iron and Glass
chain.desc: Iron ingots around glass panes, two at a time. Adding another iron ingot gives the Metal Trapdoor with no window, and black and yellow dye give the Warning Trapdoor.

notes: MACAW'S MODS SHARE ONE STRUCTURE: A SMALL NUMBER OF DISTINCT BLOCK TYPES CROSSED WITH A LARGE MATERIAL TABLE. The chain below is one step per distinct RECIPE SHAPE, not one per id, and the material tables go to wheels. MODDB: no consensus signal - moddb.json contains no key for any Macaw's mod - so every ordering here is the recipe graph alone and there is no conflict to record. Verified against mcw-trapdoors-1.1.5-mc1.20.1forge.jar (Modrinth version 1.1.5, loaders=[forge], game_versions=[1.20.1]). ID DETECTION: 191 item models, 179 blockstates, 199 lang block./item. keys; models INTERSECT lang = 191, the count used, and every one of those 191 has a recipe. THE EIGHT EXTRA LANG KEYS ARE STALE STRINGS, not missing content, and they are the trap in this jar: acacia_tropical_trapdoor, birch_paper_trapdoor, crimson_barred_trapdoor, dark_oak_four_panel_trapdoor, jungle_beach_trapdoor, oak_classic_trapdoor, spruce_cottage_trapdoor and warped_mystic_trapdoor have display names but NO item model, NO blockstate, NO recipe and NO loot table. They are exactly the wood-plus-style combinations where the STYLE IS NAMED AFTER THAT WOOD - the Classic print is made from an oak trapdoor, the Paper print from birch, the Beach print from jungle, and so on - so the mod deliberately does not register the redundant same-wood variant. Every print family is therefore ten wide, not eleven, and a generator that assumes a full 11x17 grid emits eight uncompletable quests. DISTINCT RECIPE SHAPES: 33 name-stems collapse to 8 real shapes - print, print-gated trapdoor, glass, barn (from glass), bark, barrel, raw bamboo and the three metal ones. Verified yields: print 4, print-gated trapdoor 1, glass 2, bark 2, barn 1, barrel 4, bamboo 1, metal 2, metal_full 1, metal_warning 1. WHY THE PRINTS MATTER FOR ORDERING: twelve prints exist and each one gates a whole ten-wide wood family, so mcwtrpdoors:print_classic and its siblings are genuine prerequisites and not decoration. The mod's only other lang string is mcwtrpdoors.crafting.desc = 'Crafting Ingredient', which is the prints' tooltip. DROPS: the eight stale lang keys above. Nothing was dropped as unobtainable.
